final_codebook.domain: Subtraction of fractions, mixed numbers, and whole numbers with simplification to lowest terms

skills.name: Match denominators
skills.definition: Determine a common denominator and rewrite fraction parts as equivalent fractions before subtraction when denominators are not already aligned.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a step explicitly finds an LCD or common denominator.
Tag when one or both fractions are converted to equivalent fractions to create like denominators before subtracting.
Tag in mixed-number problems when only the fractional parts are rewritten to common denominators.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when denominators are already the same and no equivalent-fraction conversion is performed.
Do not tag rewriting a whole number as a whole plus 0 over a denominator unless the step's main purpose is denominator alignment.
Do not tag borrowing/regrouping steps that convert one whole into d/d and add it to a fractional part.

skills.name: Normalize operands
skills.definition: Rewrite a whole number, fraction-bearing whole-number expression, or nonstandard mixed number into a subtraction-ready form before carrying out the subtraction.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a whole number is rewritten as a whole plus 0 over a denominator.
Tag when a mixed number with an improper fraction part is converted to an equivalent standard mixed number.
Tag when a mixed number or related expression is explicitly decomposed into whole and fractional parts to set up componentwise subtraction.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag ordinary equivalent-fraction conversion whose purpose is to create a common denominator.
Do not tag borrowing/regrouping after subtraction has produced an insufficient or negative fractional part.
Do not tag final recombination of whole and fractional parts into the answer.

skills.name: Subtract aligned fractions
skills.definition: Subtract fractions once they share a denominator by subtracting numerators and keeping the common denominator.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when two fractions with the same denominator are subtracted directly.
Tag when the fractional parts of mixed numbers are subtracted after denominators are already the same or have been aligned.
Tag whether the fractional result is positive, zero, or initially negative.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag steps whose main purpose is finding or creating a common denominator.
Do not tag subtraction of whole-number parts alone.
Do not tag simplification or final formatting unless the subtraction itself is explicitly shown.

skills.name: Subtract mixed parts
skills.definition: Subtract whole-number parts and fractional parts componentwise in mixed-number or whole-number-plus-fraction expressions before any needed regrouping.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when the solver separately computes whole-part subtraction and fraction-part subtraction.
Tag when one operand is a whole number treated as having a zero fractional part for partwise subtraction.
Tag even if the fractional difference is negative and a later borrowing step will be needed.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag pure fraction subtraction with no whole-number parts.
Do not tag the later borrowing/regrouping step that fixes an insufficient fractional part.
Do not tag final recombination alone when no componentwise subtraction is performed in that step.

skills.name: Borrow across parts
skills.definition: Regroup one whole as an equivalent fraction and add it to the fractional part when componentwise subtraction would otherwise leave an insufficient or negative fractional result.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when 1 is borrowed from the whole-number part during subtraction.
Tag when the borrowed whole is rewritten as d/d or an equivalent fractional amount and added to the existing fractional part.
Tag in mixed number minus mixed number, whole minus mixed number, or whole minus fraction contexts.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag ordinary partwise subtraction when no regrouping occurs.
Do not tag normalization of improper mixed numbers before subtraction begins.
Do not tag simplification or final expression after regrouped subtraction is complete.

skills.name: Simplify and express
skills.definition: Reduce the result to lowest terms and present it in an appropriate final form such as a fraction, mixed number, whole number, or zero.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a fraction is simplified to lowest terms.
Tag when 0 over a denominator is rewritten as 0.
Tag when whole and fractional parts are combined into a final mixed number, whole number, or other final answer form.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag setup steps such as denominator matching or operand normalization.
Do not tag subtraction or borrowing steps unless the same step also explicitly performs simplification or final recombination.
Do not tag an already-final result if no explicit simplification or expression step is shown.

decisions.details: Kept C01 as S01 Match denominators
decisions.reasoning: This skill had 3/3 consensus and is clearly independent from subtraction itself. It is diagnostically useful because some items require denominator alignment while others do not.

decisions.details: Refined C02 into S02 Normalize operands
decisions.reasoning: Although all experts agreed on the preparation concept, expert B represented only one subtype. The final definition broadens the skill to include rewriting whole numbers as n + 0/d, normalizing improper mixed numbers, and decomposing expressions into whole and fractional parts, which preserves completeness without creating overly narrow subskills.

decisions.details: Kept C03 as S03 Subtract aligned fractions
decisions.reasoning: This had 3/3 consensus and is cognitively distinct from finding common denominators. The independence principle supports keeping it separate because many items require direct subtraction with already-matched denominators.

decisions.details: Refined C04 into S04 Subtract mixed parts
decisions.reasoning: The experts agreed on componentwise subtraction in mixed-number contexts, but one version limited it to no-regrouping cases. The refined definition clarifies that the skill covers the componentwise subtraction step even when a later borrowing step is needed, improving boundary clarity and completeness.

decisions.details: Kept C05 as S05 Borrow across parts
decisions.reasoning: This had 3/3 consensus and is a distinct regrouping operation, not redundant with normalization or subtraction. It appears in a meaningful subset of items, supporting identifiability.

decisions.details: Refined C06 into S06 Simplify and express
decisions.reasoning: Experts A and C used a broader end-of-solution skill than expert B. Keeping simplification and final expression together is more minimal and better matches the dossiers, where final recombination and simplification often function as a single end-stage operation.

summary: The consolidation retained six high-consensus skills because all candidate concepts were supported by all three experts and were independently testable in the item set. Refinements focused on clarifying boundaries, especially for operand normalization, mixed-part subtraction, and the final simplify/express stage. No merges or removals were needed because the six-skill structure is already minimal, complete, and diagnostically differentiated for fraction and mixed-number subtraction.
